notice: A research QUESTION graph, not an empirical evidence graph. Hypotheses, checks and counterfactual triggers are explicitly untested. Cross-domain edges only ask questions; they never transfer efficacy claims.

nodes.statement: A subset of aging-related mechanisms is associated with replicably measurable human healthspan outcomes.
nodes.predicted_observation: Independent, appropriately controlled human studies report reproducible links between prespecified aging markers and validated healthspan endpoints.
nodes.would_count_against: Well-powered independent evidence appraisals repeatedly find no replicable association under prespecified quality criteria.

nodes.method: Plan a preregistered, literature-only evaluation of independently replicated human findings; no interventions.
nodes.evaluation_criteria: Record population, marker definition, healthspan measure, bias controls, replication status and contradictory results before making any conclusion.

nodes.question: Which independent controlled human findings contradict rather than support the proposed marker–healthspan link?

nodes.statement: Independent axolotl studies may reproduce reported links between dorsoventral patterning and Shh induction during limb regeneration.
nodes.predicted_observation: Comparable independent axolotl studies report a consistent qualitative relationship under prespecified experimental conditions.
nodes.would_count_against: Independent replication attempts fail to observe the reported association in comparable axolotl conditions.

nodes.method: Plan an observational systematic literature appraisal of published axolotl replication results only; no experiments.
nodes.evaluation_criteria: Record species, experimental conditions, assay, controls, independent replication and negative results; do not extrapolate to humans.

nodes.question: Are there independent axolotl findings that challenge the proposed patterning and Shh association?

edges.qualification: Whether nonhuman regeneration mechanisms have any relationship to human healthy aging remains unknown; no efficacy, identity, longevity, or mechanism transfers are asserted.
